title: Apache
body:
Web server software that respoonds to http requests

The *Apache HTTP Server*, and for a long time the default answer to "what serves the website".
It is the thing [[Node.js]] is compared against when the notes say Node "can be used to create
server software analogous to Apache".

The difference is where the code lives. Apache is a finished program you configure: it maps
[[URL]] paths onto files on disk, sets the [[MME]] type from the extension, handles TLS, and
hands anything dynamic off to a module such as [[PHP]]. Node is a runtime you write the server
*in*, so `http.createServer((req, resp) => {...})` is your program rather than a config file.

Its classic model is a process or thread per connection, which is where the thread-count
argument in [[PHP]] comes from. nginx and Node both exist partly to answer that with an event
loop instead.

In practice a Node app is often still put behind Apache or nginx acting as a *reverse proxy*,
which handles TLS, static files, and load spreading, and forwards the rest. See
[[Server Side]] and [[Load Balancer]].
